lessons.title: What Is Philosophy?
lessons.blurb_en: The questions that are left when the facts run out, and the method Socrates invented for working on them.
lessons.blurb_zh: 事實用完之後還剩下的問題，以及蘇格拉底為了處理這些問題發明的方法。
lessons.big_en: Philosophy is the disciplined examination of the beliefs we rely on most and question least, carried out by giving reasons and testing them.
lessons.big_zh: 哲學是對我們最依賴、卻最少質疑的信念所做的嚴格檢驗；做法是提出理由，再檢驗理由。

paras.en: A four-year-old asks why the sky is dark at night, and you answer. She asks why the sun goes away, and you answer again. By the fifth why you have usually reached one of two walls. The first wall is ignorance: there is a fact of the matter, and you do not happen to know it. The second is stranger. You have run out of facts altogether, and what is left is a question such as why there is anything at all, or how you know you are not mistaken about all of it. No further observation would settle a question like that. Philosophy is what people do at the second wall.
paras.zh: 四歲的孩子問，為什麼晚上天是黑的，你回答了。她再問太陽為什麼會走掉，你又回答了。問到第五個「為什麼」，你通常會撞上兩種牆。第一種是無知：這件事有答案，只是你剛好不知道。第二種比較奇怪：事實整個用完了，剩下的是這樣的問題——為什麼會有東西存在，而不是什麼都沒有？你怎麼知道自己不是全盤都弄錯了？再多觀察也解決不了這種問題。人在第二道牆前面做的事，就是哲學。

paras.en: The word is Greek: philosophia, from philein, to love, and sophia, wisdom. An ancient story, told by Cicero some five centuries after the supposed event, credits it to Pythagoras, who is said to have declined the title sophos, wise man, and called himself only a lover of wisdom. The story is probably legend, but it has survived because it captures something true. A philosopher is defined by a relation to wisdom, and the relation is desire rather than possession.
paras.zh: 這個字是希臘文：philosophia，由 philein（愛）與 sophia（智慧）組成。有一個古老的故事說它出自畢達哥拉斯：他不肯接受 sophos（智者）的稱號，只說自己是「愛智慧的人」。這個故事是西塞羅在事隔約五百年後記下的，多半是傳說；它流傳下來，是因為說中了一件事。哲學家是由他跟智慧的關係來界定的，而那個關係是渴望，不是擁有。

paras.en: Plato has Socrates say that “philosophy begins in wonder” (Theaetetus 155d), and Aristotle agreed: “it is owing to their wonder that men both now begin and at first began to philosophize” (Metaphysics 982b). The wonder they had in mind is not the pleasant awe of a sunset. It is closer to puzzlement, the discomfort of noticing that something you took to be obvious does not, on inspection, make sense. Everyone knows what time is until asked to say. Everyone knows what a fair share is until two people claim the same thing.
paras.zh: 柏拉圖筆下的蘇格拉底說「哲學始於驚奇」（《泰阿泰德篇》155d），亞里斯多德也同意：「人們現在開始、以及最初開始做哲學思考，都是由於驚奇」（《形上學》982b）。他們說的驚奇，不是看夕陽時那種愉快的讚嘆，比較接近困惑：你發現一件向來以為理所當然的事，仔細一看竟然說不通，心裡因此不安。人人都知道時間是什麼，直到有人要他說出來。人人都知道什麼叫公平的一份，直到兩個人要同一樣東西。

paras.en: Socrates (c. 470–399 BCE) made a method of that discomfort. He wrote nothing. What we have are portraits by people who knew him, above all Plato, and in those portraits he does one thing again and again: he finds someone who claims to know what courage or justice or piety is, asks for a definition, and tests it against cases the speaker himself accepts. A general says that courage is standing firm in the line; Socrates points out that soldiers sometimes fight bravely while retreating. The definition is revised, tested again, and fails again.
paras.zh: 蘇格拉底（約西元前 470–399 年）把這種不安變成一套方法。他一個字也沒寫。我們有的是認識他的人為他畫的像，其中最重要的是柏拉圖；在這些畫像裡，他反覆做同一件事：找到一個自稱知道什麼是勇敢、正義或虔敬的人，請對方下定義，再拿對方自己也承認的例子來檢驗這個定義。一位將軍說，勇敢就是在陣線上堅守不退；蘇格拉底指出，士兵有時是一邊撤退一邊英勇作戰的。定義修改了，再受檢驗，又垮了。

paras.en: The technical name for this cross-examination is the elenchus, and its usual result is aporia, a state of being at a loss. Socrates considered that result a gain. A person who has discovered that he does not know is at least in a position to start looking.
paras.zh: 這種詰問的術語叫 elenchus（詰問法），通常的結果是 aporia，也就是不知所措、無路可走的狀態。蘇格拉底認為這個結果是收穫。一個人發現自己並不知道，至少就站到了可以開始尋找的位置。

paras.en: Three neighbors help to mark the borders. Philosophy is not science, because its questions are not settled by measurement, though it reasons about what measurement can show. It is not religion, because it accepts no conclusion on authority, though it asks many of the same questions. And it is not mere opinion, because a philosophical claim has to be argued for, and an argument can be checked by anyone.
paras.zh: 有三個鄰居可以幫我們標出邊界。哲學不是科學，因為它的問題不是靠測量解決的，雖然它會推敲測量到底能證明什麼。哲學不是宗教，因為它不憑權威接受任何結論，雖然它問的許多問題跟宗教相同。哲學也不只是意見，因為哲學主張必須有論證支持，而論證是任何人都能檢查的。

paras.en: The discipline lives on that last point. You are free to believe whatever you like, but once you give reasons, your reasons become public property, and other people may show you that they do not support what you thought they did.
paras.zh: 這門學問就靠最後這一點活著。你愛相信什麼都可以；可是一旦你給出理由，你的理由就成了公共財，別人可以指給你看：這些理由並不支持你以為它們支持的結論。

paras.en: Over twenty-five centuries the questions have sorted themselves into branches. Logic studies what follows from what. Epistemology asks what knowledge is and whether we have any. Metaphysics asks what there is and what it is like: time, causation, the self, free will. Ethics asks how one should live, political philosophy how we should live together, and aesthetics what beauty and art are. Around these have grown the “philosophies of”: of mind, of language, of science, of religion, of education. The borders are porous. Ask whether a machine can think, and within a few minutes you will be doing metaphysics, epistemology, and ethics at once.
paras.zh: 兩千五百年下來，這些問題自己分成了幾個分支。邏輯學研究什麼可以從什麼推出來。知識論問知識是什麼、我們到底有沒有知識。形上學問有什麼東西存在、它們是什麼樣子：時間、因果、自我、自由意志。倫理學問人應該怎麼活，政治哲學問我們應該怎麼一起活，美學問美與藝術是什麼。在這些周圍又長出一批「某某哲學」：心靈哲學、語言哲學、科學哲學、宗教哲學、教育哲學。分支之間的邊界是透水的。問一句「機器會不會思考」，幾分鐘之內你就同時在做形上學、知識論和倫理學了。

paras.en: The Greek word should not mislead us about ownership. Confucius died about a decade before Socrates was born, and by then he had spent a lifetime asking what makes a person humane. The Buddha, whose dates are less certain, taught in the same era that what we call a self is a process and not a thing. Neither had a word for “philosophy.” The Chinese term 哲學 was coined only in 1874, by the Japanese scholar Nishi Amane, to translate the European word.
paras.zh: 這個字是希臘文，但我們不該因此弄錯這門學問歸誰所有。孔子過世大約十年後蘇格拉底才出生，而孔子已經用了一輩子追問：什麼使一個人成為仁者。佛陀的年代比較不確定，但他在同一個時代教導：我們稱為「我」的，是一個過程，不是一個東西。他們兩位都沒有「哲學」這個詞。中文的「哲學」要到 1874 年才出現，是日本學者西周為了翻譯這個歐洲字而造的。

paras.en: Yet a tradition does not need the label to do the work. Wherever people have given reasons for claims about knowledge, reality, and the good life, and have answered objections to them, philosophy has been going on. This series therefore follows three lines, Greek, Chinese, and Indian, and pays attention to the places where they meet.
paras.zh: 不過，一個傳統不需要有這個標籤，也能做這件工作。只要有人為自己關於知識、真實與美好人生的主張提出理由，並且回應別人的反駁，哲學就在進行。所以這個系列沿著三條線走：希臘、中國、印度，並且特別留意它們相遇的地方。

paras.en: Bertrand Russell faced the obvious complaint, that philosophy never seems to settle anything, and gave two replies. First, the complaint is partly an illusion: when a philosophical question becomes answerable, it gets a new name. Physics was once “natural philosophy”; psychology left home in the nineteenth century. What remains under the old name is, by definition, the unfinished business.
paras.zh: 最常見的抱怨是：哲學好像從來沒有解決過任何問題。羅素正面回應了這個抱怨，給了兩個答覆。第一，這個抱怨有一部分是錯覺：一個哲學問題一旦變得可以回答，就會換一個名字。物理學從前叫「自然哲學」；心理學是十九世紀才離家的。還留在舊名字底下的，按定義就是沒做完的事。

paras.en: Second, the unfinished business is worth doing for its own sake. Philosophy, he wrote, is to be studied “not for the sake of any definite answers to its questions,” but “for the sake of the questions themselves; because these questions enlarge our conception of what is possible.” A mind that has never doubted its own assumptions is confined by them. Socrates put the point more severely at his trial. The unexamined life, he told the jury, is not worth living.
paras.zh: 第二，沒做完的事本身就值得做。他寫道，研究哲學「不是為了它的問題有什麼確定的答案」，而是「為了這些問題本身；因為這些問題擴大了我們對於什麼是可能的想像」。一個從來沒有懷疑過自己預設的心靈，就被這些預設關住了。蘇格拉底在受審時把話說得更重。他對陪審團說：沒有經過省察的人生，不值得活。

lab.title_zh: 親手做一次：蘇格拉底式詰問
lab.lead_en: Three questions Socrates actually asked, with the answers his companions actually gave. Choose the definition you find most convincing and see what happens to it. Every step follows a dialogue of Plato; the reference is given under each reply.
lab.lead_zh: 這是蘇格拉底真的問過的三個問題，以及對話者真的給過的答案。選一個你覺得最有說服力的定義，看它會遇到什麼。每一步都依據柏拉圖的對話錄，出處標在每段回應下方。

dialogues.who_en: Socrates is talking with two Athenian generals, Laches and Nicias.
dialogues.who_zh: 蘇格拉底在跟兩位雅典將軍談話：拉凱斯與尼基亞斯。

defs.en: Courage is staying at your post and not running from the enemy.
defs.zh: 勇敢就是堅守崗位，不從敵人面前逃走。
defs.re_en: Then what about soldiers who fight while falling back? The Scythian horsemen fight as they retreat, and the Spartans at Plataea gave ground, then turned and won. And courage is not confined to battle: people are brave at sea, in illness, in poverty, and against their own desires. You have given me one kind of courage. I asked what all of them have in common.
defs.re_zh: 那麼一邊後退一邊作戰的士兵呢？斯基泰騎兵是邊退邊打的；斯巴達人在普拉提亞先讓出陣地，再回頭取勝。而且勇敢不限於戰場：人在海上、在病中、在貧困裡、在對抗自己的欲望時，都可以是勇敢的。你給我的是其中一種勇敢。我問的是它們全部的共同點。

defs.en: Courage is a kind of endurance of the soul.
defs.zh: 勇敢是靈魂的一種堅忍。
defs.re_en: You agree that courage is always something noble. But endurance can be foolish: a man who stubbornly holds on to a hopeless and harmful course is enduring, and we do not admire him. If foolish endurance counts, then courage is sometimes shameful, which you deny. So endurance alone cannot be what courage is.
defs.re_zh: 你同意勇敢永遠是高貴的。可是堅忍可以是愚蠢的：一個人固執地堅持一條沒有希望、而且有害的路，他是在堅忍，但我們並不欽佩他。如果愚蠢的堅忍也算，那勇敢有時就是可恥的，而這是你否認的。所以單是堅忍，不可能就是勇敢。

defs.en: Courage is knowledge of what is to be feared and what is to be hoped for.
defs.zh: 勇敢是一種知識：知道什麼該怕、什麼可以期待。
defs.flaw: Proves too much · 證明過頭
defs.re_en: What is to be feared is future evil, and what is to be hoped for is future good. But knowledge of good and evil is not divided by time; whoever has it knows past, present, and future goods and evils alike. A person with that knowledge would lack nothing of virtue: he would be just, temperate, and pious as well. So you have defined the whole of virtue, and we agreed at the start that courage is only a part of it.
defs.re_zh: 該怕的是未來的惡，可以期待的是未來的善。可是關於善惡的知識不分時間；有這種知識的人，對過去、現在、未來的善惡一樣明白。有這種知識的人，在德行上什麼都不缺：他同時也會是正義的、節制的、虔敬的。所以你定義的是德行的全部，而我們一開始就同意，勇敢只是德行的一部分。

dialogues.end_en: “Then, Nicias, we have not discovered what courage is.” The dialogue ends there. Two generals who have shown courage all their lives cannot say what it is.
dialogues.end_zh: 「那麼，尼基亞斯，我們還沒有發現勇敢是什麼。」對話到此結束。兩位一輩子都表現出勇敢的將軍，說不出勇敢是什麼。

dialogues.who_en: Socrates is at the house of the old merchant Cephalus, with his son Polemarchus and the sophist Thrasymachus.
dialogues.who_zh: 蘇格拉底在老商人克法洛斯家中，在場的還有他的兒子波勒馬科斯與智者特拉敘馬科斯。

defs.en: Justice is telling the truth and giving back what you owe.
defs.zh: 正義就是說實話，並且歸還你所欠的。
defs.re_en: Suppose a friend lends you his weapon while he is in his right mind, and asks for it back after he has gone mad. Everyone would say that you ought not to return it, and that you ought not to tell him the whole truth either. So there are cases where returning what you owe is the unjust thing to do, and the definition fails.
defs.re_zh: 假設一位朋友在神智清楚的時候把武器借給你，後來他發瘋了，回來向你討。誰都會說你不該還給他，也不該把全部實情告訴他。可見有些時候，歸還所欠的東西反而是不義的，這個定義不成立。

defs.en: Justice is doing good to your friends and harm to your enemies.
defs.zh: 正義就是對朋友行善、對敵人加害。
defs.flaw: Leads to absurdity · 推出荒謬
defs.re_en: We often misjudge people, and take the good for enemies and the bad for friends; then your justice would have us harm the good. And consider what harming does. A horse that is harmed becomes a worse horse, and a person who is harmed becomes worse in human excellence, that is, less just. Can it be the work of justice to make people unjust? Heat does not cool things, and the just person does not make anyone worse.
defs.re_zh: 我們常常看錯人，把好人當敵人、把壞人當朋友；那麼照你的正義，我們就該去傷害好人。再想想「加害」做了什麼：馬受了傷害，就成為一匹更差的馬；人受了傷害，在人的優秀品質上就變得更差，也就是更不正義。使人變得不正義，會是正義的工作嗎？熱不會使東西變冷，正義的人也不會使任何人變壞。

defs.en: Justice is nothing but the advantage of the stronger.
defs.zh: 正義不過是強者的利益。
defs.re_en: You say the rulers make laws for their own advantage, and that it is just for subjects to obey. But rulers are not infallible. Sometimes they mistake their own interest and command what harms them. On your account it is just to obey those commands too. So it is just to do what is to the advantage of the stronger, and also just to do what is to their disadvantage.
defs.re_zh: 你說統治者為了自己的利益立法，而臣民服從就是正義。可是統治者不是不會犯錯的。有時他們誤判自己的利益，下了對自己有害的命令。照你的說法，服從這些命令也是正義的。那麼，做對強者有利的事是正義，做對強者不利的事也是正義。

dialogues.end_en: Book I ends with Socrates admitting that he has feasted on arguments without ever settling what justice is. The other nine books of the Republic are his second attempt.
dialogues.end_zh: 第一卷結尾，蘇格拉底承認自己把論證嘗了個遍，卻始終沒有弄清楚正義是什麼。《理想國》其餘九卷，是他的第二次嘗試。

dialogues.who_en: Socrates, on his way to answer the charge of impiety, meets Euthyphro, who is prosecuting his own father for murder and is certain that this is the pious thing to do.
dialogues.who_zh: 蘇格拉底正要去應訊「不敬神」的指控，途中遇到歐緒弗洛。歐緒弗洛正要控告自己的父親殺人，而且確信這樣做才是虔敬。

defs.en: Piety is doing as I am doing: prosecuting the wrongdoer, whoever he may be.
defs.zh: 虔敬就是做我現在做的事：告發犯罪的人，不管他是誰。
defs.flaw: An example, not a definition · 是例子，不是定義
defs.re_en: I did not ask you for one or two of the many pious acts. I asked for the form itself that makes all pious acts pious, so that I can look to it as a standard and say of any act whether it is of that kind. You have told me that this is pious. You have not told me what piety is.
defs.re_zh: 我問的不是許多虔敬行為當中的一兩件。我問的是使一切虔敬行為成為虔敬的那個「形式」本身，好讓我拿它當標準，判斷任何一個行為屬不屬於這一類。你告訴了我「這件事是虔敬的」，還沒有告訴我「虔敬是什麼」。

defs.en: Piety is what is dear to the gods.
defs.re_en: By your own account the gods quarrel, and what they quarrel about is the just and the unjust, the good and the bad. Then the same act will be loved by some gods and hated by others, and it will be pious and impious at once. Your own prosecution may please Zeus and offend Cronos.
defs.re_zh: 照你自己的說法，諸神彼此爭吵，而他們爭的正是公不公正、善不善。那麼同一個行為會被某些神喜愛、被另一些神憎恨，它就同時是虔敬的又是不虔敬的。你這場告發，也許宙斯喜歡，克洛諾斯卻不高興。

defs.en: Piety is what all the gods love.
defs.zh: 虔敬就是所有的神都喜愛的。
defs.flaw: The Euthyphro dilemma · 歐緒弗洛兩難
defs.re_en: Is the pious loved by the gods because it is pious, or is it pious because it is loved by the gods? You say the first. But then being loved by the gods is something that happens to piety, a consequence of what it already is. You have told me a fact about piety and left its nature untouched. If you say the second, anything at all would become pious the moment the gods happened to love it.
defs.re_zh: 虔敬的事，是因為它虔敬所以被神喜愛，還是因為被神喜愛所以它虔敬？你說是前者。可是這樣一來，「被神喜愛」只是發生在虔敬身上的一件事，是它本來是什麼的結果。你告訴了我關於虔敬的一個事實，卻沒有碰到它的本質。如果你說是後者，那麼任何事情只要神碰巧喜愛，就立刻變成虔敬的了。

dialogues.end_en: Euthyphro says he is in a hurry and leaves. The question he could not answer, whether something is good because it is commanded or commanded because it is good, is still argued over in ethics and theology.
dialogues.end_zh: 歐緒弗洛說他趕時間，走了。他答不出來的那個問題——一件事是因為被命令所以善，還是因為善所以被命令——至今仍是倫理學與神學爭論的題目。

tests.en: Is it a definition, or only an example? A list of brave acts does not say what makes them brave.
tests.zh: 它是定義，還是只是例子？列出幾件勇敢的事，並沒有說出是什麼使它們勇敢。

tests.en: Is it too narrow? Look for a clear case of the thing that the definition leaves out.
tests.zh: 它是不是太窄？找一個明明屬於這個概念、卻被定義排除在外的例子。

tests.en: Is it too broad? Look for something the definition lets in that plainly does not belong.
tests.zh: 它是不是太寬？找一個明明不屬於這個概念、卻被定義放進來的例子。

tests.en: Is it circular? Check whether the word being defined, or a near synonym, has slipped into the definition.
tests.zh: 它是不是循環？檢查被定義的那個詞，或它的近義詞，有沒有溜進定義裡。

tests.en: Does it conflict with something else you believe? If it does, one of the two has to go.
tests.zh: 它跟你相信的別的事衝不衝突？如果衝突，兩者之中總得放棄一個。

lab.own_en: Now write your own definition of friendship, fairness, or respect, and run the five tests on it. Nothing you type leaves this page.
lab.own_zh: 現在換你：替「友誼」「公平」或「尊重」寫一個自己的定義，再用上面五個問題檢驗它。你輸入的內容不會離開這個頁面。

argument.lead_en: Why should anyone submit to this treatment? Socrates’ answer at his trial can be set out as an argument. Click a premise to see what can be said against it.
argument.lead_zh: 為什麼要讓自己受這種詰問？蘇格拉底在法庭上的回答，可以攤開成一個論證。點任何一個前提，看看別人可以怎麼反對它。

steps.en: To live well, a person needs true beliefs about what matters: what is just, what is brave, what is good.
steps.zh: 要活得好，人需要對重要的事有正確的信念：什麼是正義、什麼是勇敢、什麼是善。
steps.ob_en: Rarely attacked. One could deny it by holding that living well is a matter of habit or good fortune, and that belief has little to do with it.
steps.ob_zh: 很少被攻擊。要否認它，可以主張活得好靠的是習慣或運氣，跟信念沒有多大關係。

steps.en: Most of our beliefs about these things were absorbed from family and city, and have never been tested. Untested beliefs may be false, or may contradict one another, without our noticing.
steps.zh: 我們對這些事的信念，多半是從家庭與城邦吸收來的，從來沒有受過檢驗。沒受過檢驗的信念可能是錯的，也可能互相矛盾，而我們自己不會發現。
steps.ob_en: The elenchus itself is the evidence for this premise: generals cannot define courage, and a religious expert cannot define piety.
steps.ob_zh: 詰問法本身就是這個前提的證據：將軍定義不出勇敢，宗教專家定義不出虔敬。

steps.en: The only way to find out which beliefs survive is to examine them: state them, give reasons, and face objections.
steps.zh: 要知道哪些信念站得住，唯一的辦法是省察它們：說出來、給理由、面對反駁。
steps.ob_en: A traditionalist may reply that long experience has already tested inherited beliefs, and tested them better than one person’s reasoning can. This is roughly Edmund Burke’s defense of “prejudice.”
steps.ob_zh: 傳統主義者可以回答：世代累積的經驗已經檢驗過這些繼承來的信念，而且比一個人的推理檢驗得更好。這大致是柏克為「成見」所做的辯護。

steps.en: Therefore a life without examination leaves living well to luck. In Socrates’ stronger words, it is “not worth living.”
steps.zh: 所以，不經省察的人生，把「活得好」交給了運氣。用蘇格拉底更重的話說，這樣的人生「不值得活」。
steps.ob_en: This is the step most often attacked. The premises support the weaker conclusion at most. Many people who never philosophize are kind, brave, and content, and it seems false, even arrogant, to say their lives are not worth living.
steps.ob_zh: 這是最常被攻擊的一步。前提頂多支持那個比較弱的結論。許多從不做哲學思考的人善良、勇敢、知足；說他們的人生不值得活，似乎是錯的，甚至是傲慢的。

source.lead_en: The Apology is Plato’s version of the speech Socrates gave at his trial in 399 BCE. (Apologia means a defense in court; he apologizes for nothing.) Two short passages carry the lesson.
source.lead_zh: 《申辯篇》是柏拉圖筆下，蘇格拉底在西元前 399 年受審時的發言。（apologia 是法庭上的「辯護」，他什麼歉也沒道。）兩小段話就帶出了這一課的重點。

passages.en: Well, although I do not suppose that either of us knows anything really beautiful and good, I am better off than he is,—for he knows nothing, and thinks that he knows; I neither know nor think that I know. In this latter particular, then, I seem to have slightly the advantage of him.
passages.zh: 好吧，雖然我不認為我們兩人當中有誰真的知道什麼美與善的事，我還是比他好一點：他什麼都不知道，卻以為自己知道；我既不知道，也不以為自己知道。就在後面這一點上，我似乎比他略勝一籌。
passages.note_en: Notice how modest the claim is. He does not say “I know that I know nothing,” which would contradict itself. He says he does not think he knows what he does not know, and that this gives him a slight advantage.
passages.note_zh: 注意這個說法有多節制。他沒有說「我知道我一無所知」，那句話會自相矛盾。他說的是：我不知道的事，我不以為自己知道；而這只讓他「略勝一籌」。

passages.en: …and if I say again that daily to discourse about virtue, and of those other things about which you hear me examining myself and others, is the greatest good of man, and that the unexamined life is not worth living, you are still less likely to believe me.
passages.zh: ……如果我又說，每天談論德行，談論你們聽到我省察自己、也省察別人的那些事，是人最大的善；而未經省察的人生不值得活——你們就更不會相信我了。
passages.note_en: The famous line sits in a subordinate clause, inside a sentence about not being believed. He has just been found guilty and is explaining why he will not accept exile on condition of silence. Note also “examining myself and others”: the examination is turned on himself first.
passages.note_zh: 這句名言其實藏在一個子句裡，而整個句子講的是「你們不會相信我」。他剛被判有罪，正在解釋為什麼不接受「閉嘴就可以流亡」的條件。也注意「省察自己、也省察別人」：省察的對象，先是他自己。

items.o_en: Philosophy makes no progress. After twenty-five centuries philosophers still disagree about everything, while a first-year physics student knows more than Newton did.
items.o_zh: 哲學沒有進步。兩千五百年了，哲學家還是什麼都吵不出結論；而一個大一物理系學生知道的，已經比牛頓多。
items.r_en: Russell’s reply is that solved problems are renamed and leave the field, so what remains is always the unsolved part. A second reply is that progress in philosophy is often negative: we now know why a great many tempting answers fail, and that is knowledge. A critic may fairly press the point, however. If no positive answer has ever been secured, on what grounds do we call the activity a form of inquiry at all?
items.r_zh: 羅素的回答是：解決了的問題會改名、離開這個領域，所以留下來的永遠是沒解決的那一部分。第二個回答是，哲學的進步常常是否定式的：我們現在知道許多誘人的答案為什麼不成立，而這就是知識。不過批評者可以合理地追問下去：如果從來沒有一個正面的答案站穩過，我們憑什麼說這是一種「探究」？

items.o_en: The elenchus only destroys. Socrates refutes every answer and offers none, and his victims leave humiliated, having learned nothing.
items.o_zh: 詰問法只會破壞。蘇格拉底駁倒每一個答案，自己卻不給答案；被他問倒的人顏面盡失地離開，什麼也沒學到。
items.r_en: In the Meno, Socrates leads a boy to see that his confident answer to a geometry problem is wrong, and then asks whether the boy is worse off for it. Before, he thought he knew and would not have looked for the answer; now he knows that he does not know, and wants to find out (Meno 84a–c). Clearing away false confidence is the first step of learning. Whether Socrates took that step kindly is another matter, and Athens evidently thought he did not.
items.r_zh: 在《美諾篇》裡，蘇格拉底帶一個少年看出他對一道幾何題的自信答案是錯的，然後問：這個少年因此變糟了嗎？先前他以為自己知道，所以不會去找答案；現在他知道自己不知道，而且想弄清楚（《美諾篇》84a–c）。清掉虛假的自信，是學習的第一步。至於蘇格拉底做這一步的時候夠不夠厚道，那是另一回事；雅典人顯然認為他不夠。

items.o_en: “The unexamined life is not worth living” is elitist. It condemns most of the human beings who have ever lived.
items.o_zh: 「未經省察的人生不值得活」是菁英主義，它等於否定了有史以來絕大多數人的人生。
items.r_en: One defense reads the line narrowly: Socrates is speaking of himself, explaining why he could not live silenced. Another reads “examined” modestly, as the ordinary practice of asking whether you are living as you think you should, which requires no schooling. On either reading the claim is easier to defend than the slogan suggests. Read at full strength, as a verdict on other people’s lives, it is very hard to defend.
items.r_zh: 一種辯護把這句話讀得很窄：蘇格拉底是在說他自己，在解釋為什麼他沒辦法閉著嘴活下去。另一種辯護把「省察」讀得很平實：就是平常問問自己，是不是照著自己認為應該的方式在活；這不需要讀過書。照這兩種讀法，這個主張都比那句口號容易辯護。但如果照字面的全部力道，把它讀成對別人人生的判決，就很難辯護了。

said.en: This sentence appears nowhere in Plato. It is a later compression of Apology 21d, where Socrates says only that he does not think he knows what he does not know. The compressed version is also self-defeating, since it claims to know something. The Latin tag often quoted for it, scio me nihil scire, is likewise a later formulation.
said.zh: 柏拉圖的著作裡找不到這句話。它是後人把《申辯篇》21d 濃縮而成的；蘇格拉底在那裡只說，他不知道的事，他不以為自己知道。濃縮版還會自打嘴巴，因為它宣稱「知道」了一件事。常被引用的拉丁文版本 scio me nihil scire，同樣是後來才有的說法。

terms.d_en: The examination, by argument, of basic questions about knowledge, reality, and value.
terms.d_zh: 以論證的方式，檢驗關於知識、真實與價值的基本問題。

terms.d_en: Socrates’ method: draw out a definition, then show that it conflicts with other things the speaker believes.
terms.d_zh: 蘇格拉底的方法：引出一個定義，再指出它跟說話者相信的其他事互相衝突。

terms.d_en: The state of being at a loss when every proposed answer has failed.
terms.d_zh: 所有提出的答案都失敗之後，那種不知所措的狀態。

terms.d_en: The branch that studies knowledge, belief, and justification.
terms.d_zh: 研究知識、信念與證成的分支。

terms.o: Gk. ta meta ta physika, ‘the books after the Physics’
terms.d_en: The branch that studies what exists and its most general features. The name began as a librarian’s label for where Aristotle’s treatise was shelved.
terms.d_zh: 研究什麼存在、以及存在物最普遍特徵的分支。這個名字原本只是圖書編目的標籤，指亞里斯多德那部書排在《物理學》之後。

terms.d_en: The branch that studies how one ought to live and act.
terms.d_zh: 研究人應該怎麼生活、怎麼行動的分支。

terms.d_en: A set of premises offered in support of a conclusion. In philosophy the word never means a quarrel.
terms.d_zh: 用來支持一個結論的一組前提。在哲學裡，這個字從來不是「吵架」的意思。

terms.d_en: A single case that shows a general claim to be false.
terms.d_zh: 足以證明一個普遍主張為假的單一個案。

vocab.eg: No further observation would settle a question like that.
vocab.eg_zh: 再多觀察也解決不了這種問題。

vocab.eg: An ancient story credits the word to Pythagoras.
vocab.eg_zh: 一個古老的故事把這個字歸給畢達哥拉斯。

vocab.eg: Something you took to be obvious does not, on inspection, make sense.
vocab.eg_zh: 你以為理所當然的事，仔細一看竟說不通。

vocab.eg: Aporia is a state of being at a loss.
vocab.eg_zh: Aporia 是一種不知所措的狀態。

vocab.eg: Philosophy accepts no conclusion on authority.
vocab.eg_zh: 哲學不憑權威接受任何結論。

vocab.eg: The borders between the branches are porous.
vocab.eg_zh: 各分支之間的邊界並不嚴密。

vocab.eg: The term was coined only in 1874.
vocab.eg_zh: 這個詞直到 1874 年才被造出來。

vocab.eg: What remains under the old name is the unfinished business.
vocab.eg_zh: 留在舊名字底下的，是還沒做完的事。

vocab.zh: 為了它本身（而非別的目的）
vocab.eg: The unfinished business is worth doing for its own sake.
vocab.eg_zh: 這些沒做完的事，本身就值得做。

vocab.eg: A mind that has never doubted its assumptions is confined by them.
vocab.eg_zh: 從未懷疑過自己預設的心靈，就被這些預設關住了。

quiz.q: According to the essay, what distinguishes the “second wall” from the first?
options: No further observation could settle the question.
The answer exists, but only experts know it.
The question is asked by a child.
The question concerns religion.

quiz.q: Why does Socrates regard aporia as a gain?
options: Someone who knows that he does not know is in a position to start looking.
It proves that definitions are impossible.
It shows that the other speaker is a fool.
It ends the conversation quickly.

quiz.q: What is wrong with Euthyphro’s first answer, “piety is doing as I am doing”?
options: It gives an example where a definition was asked for.
It is circular.
It contradicts what the gods have said.
It is too broad.
I do not think I know what I do not know.
I know that I know nothing.
No one can know anything.
I am the wisest man in Athens.

quiz.q: What is Russell’s first reply to the charge that philosophy settles nothing?
options: Questions that become answerable are renamed as sciences and leave philosophy.
Philosophy has in fact settled most of its questions.
Definite answers do not matter to anyone.
Science has not settled anything either.

write.en: Pick a word you use every day (friend, fair, success) and write a one-sentence definition. Then write the strongest counterexample you can find, and revise the definition once.
write.zh: 選一個你天天在用的詞（朋友、公平、成功），用一句話下定義。接著寫出你想得到的最強反例，再把定義修改一次。

write.en: Is the unexamined life really “not worth living”? Defend either the strong claim or the weaker one in about 150 words, and answer one objection.
write.zh: 未經省察的人生真的「不值得活」嗎？用大約 150 個英文字，為強的主張或弱的主張辯護，並回應一個反駁。

write.en: Russell says that solved philosophical problems are renamed as sciences. Name one question that you think will never make that move, and say why.
write.zh: 羅素說，解決了的哲學問題會改名成為科學。舉出一個你認為永遠不會「搬家」的問題，並說明理由。

paras.en: The Buddha was also a master of the question. An early discourse (Aṅguttara Nikāya 4.42) sorts questions into four kinds: those to be answered directly, those to be answered after drawing distinctions, those to be answered with a counter-question, and those to be set aside. The third kind is what Socrates did for a living, and the second, vibhajja, “analysis,” gave one early school its name.
paras.zh: 佛陀也是提問的大師。早期的一部經（《增支部》4.42）把問題分成四種：應當直接回答的（一向記）、應當分別之後再回答的（分別記）、應當反問之後再回答的（反詰記）、應當擱置不答的（捨置記）。第三種正是蘇格拉底終身在做的事；第二種「分別」（vibhajja），後來成了早期一個部派的名字。

paras.en: The fourth kind marks the real difference. Socrates held that examination is itself the good life, and he pursued a question wherever it led. The Buddha set certain questions aside, among them whether the world is eternal and whether it is finite, on the ground that pursuing them does not lead to the end of suffering. For him, inquiry is governed by a practical aim. Whether that restriction is a limit on philosophy or a philosophical position in its own right is a question this series will return to (Dharma and the West, D21).
paras.zh: 第四種才是真正的差別所在。蘇格拉底認為省察本身就是美好的人生，問題走到哪裡他就追到哪裡。佛陀則把某些問題擱在一邊，例如世界是不是永恆、是不是有邊，理由是追究這些問題並不導向苦的止息。對佛陀來說，探究受一個實踐目的節制。這個限制到底是對哲學的限縮，還是本身就是一種哲學立場？這個系列之後會回來談（佛法與西方哲學 D21）。

philosophers.name: Socrates
philosophers.tag_en: The man who wrote nothing and changed what philosophy is about.
philosophers.tag_zh: 一個字也沒寫，卻改變了哲學在問什麼的人。
facts: Sophroniscus, a stoneworker; Phaenarete, a midwife

paras.en: Socrates was born around 470 BCE, when Athens was becoming the richest and most confident city in Greece. His father, Sophroniscus, is said to have worked in stone; his mother, Phaenarete, was a midwife, a fact Plato later turned into a metaphor. He was not rich and not handsome. His friends compared him to a satyr: snub nose, bulging eyes, the same old cloak in every season, and no shoes.
paras.zh: 蘇格拉底大約生於西元前 470 年，當時雅典正要成為希臘最富有、最有自信的城邦。據說他的父親索弗羅尼斯科斯是石匠；母親費納瑞特是接生婆，這件事後來被柏拉圖變成一個比喻。他不富有，也不好看。朋友拿他比作森林裡的薩提爾：塌鼻、凸眼，一年四季同一件舊斗篷，而且不穿鞋。

paras.en: He served as a heavy infantryman in three campaigns of the long war with Sparta, at Potidaea, Delium, and Amphipolis. The young aristocrat Alcibiades, whose life he saved at Potidaea, reported that Socrates endured cold and hunger better than anyone and walked off the lost field at Delium so calmly that no enemy cared to approach him.
paras.zh: 在對斯巴達的長年戰爭中，他以重裝步兵的身分參加過三場戰役：波提狄亞、德里昂、安菲波利斯。年輕貴族阿爾基比亞德在波提狄亞被他救過一命；據他說，蘇格拉底比誰都耐寒耐餓，而德里昂兵敗撤退時，他走得那樣從容，敵人沒有一個想靠近。

paras.en: At his trial Socrates explained how his odd career began. His friend Chaerephon had asked the oracle at Delphi whether anyone was wiser than Socrates, and the priestess had answered that no one was. Socrates, aware of having “no wisdom, small or great,” set out to refute the god by finding a wiser man. He questioned politicians, poets, and craftsmen, and found that each believed he knew things he did not. He concluded that the oracle meant something modest: he was wiser only in not mistaking his ignorance for knowledge.
paras.zh: 蘇格拉底在法庭上解釋過，他那古怪的生涯是怎麼開始的。他的朋友凱勒豐去德爾菲問神諭：有沒有人比蘇格拉底更有智慧？女祭司回答說沒有。蘇格拉底自知「大小智慧都沒有」，就動身去找一個更有智慧的人，想藉此反駁神。他問過政治家、詩人、工匠，發現每一個都以為自己知道一些其實不知道的事。他的結論是，神諭的意思很平實：他比較有智慧，只在於他沒有把自己的無知誤認為知識。

paras.en: From then on he spent his days in the agora and the gymnasia, questioning anyone who would stop. He charged no fee, which set him apart from the professional teachers called sophists, and he denied that he taught anything at all. He compared himself to a gadfly sent to sting a large and sluggish horse, and to a midwife who helps others deliver ideas while having none of her own.
paras.zh: 從那以後，他整天待在市集與體育場，逢人就問，只要對方肯停下來。他不收學費，這一點使他跟那些稱為「智者」的職業教師不同；他甚至否認自己教過任何東西。他把自己比作一隻牛虻，被派來叮一匹龐大而遲鈍的馬；又比作接生婆，幫別人把想法生出來，自己卻沒有孩子。

paras.en: Athens lost the war in 404 BCE and endured a brutal oligarchy, the Thirty, several of whose leaders had once kept company with Socrates. Socrates himself had defied them: ordered to arrest an innocent man, Leon of Salamis, he simply went home. Democracy was restored the next year, and in 399 three citizens, Meletus, Anytus, and Lycon, brought him to court. The charge, in Plato’s wording, was that he “corrupts the youth” and “does not believe in the gods of the state, but has other new divinities of his own.”
paras.zh: 西元前 404 年雅典戰敗，接著經歷了殘暴的寡頭統治「三十人僭主」，其中幾位領袖從前跟蘇格拉底來往過。蘇格拉底自己倒是違抗過他們：他們命令他去逮捕一個無辜的人，薩拉米斯的勒翁，他直接回家了。第二年民主政體恢復；西元前 399 年，美勒托斯、安尼托斯、呂孔三位公民把他告上法庭。照柏拉圖的記載，罪名是他「敗壞青年」，並且「不信城邦所信的神，另立自己的新神」。

paras.en: A jury of several hundred citizens found him guilty by a narrow margin; had thirty votes gone the other way, he says, he would have been acquitted. Asked to propose his own penalty, he suggested free meals at public expense, then a small fine. The jury chose death. He refused a chance to escape, arguing that a citizen who has accepted the laws all his life may not break them when they turn against him, and a month later he drank the hemlock among his friends. In Plato’s account his last words were a reminder to pay a debt: “Crito, we owe a cock to Asclepius.”
paras.zh: 由數百位公民組成的陪審團以些微差距判他有罪；他說，只要有三十票投向另一邊，他就無罪了。輪到他自己提議刑罰時，他先提議由公家供他免費用餐，後來才改口說可以繳一筆小額罰金。陪審團選了死刑。他拒絕了逃亡的機會，理由是：一個公民一輩子都接受法律，就不能在法律轉而對他不利的時候違反它。一個月後，他在朋友圍繞之下喝了毒芹汁。照柏拉圖的記述，他最後一句話是提醒朋友還一筆債：「克里托，我們還欠阿斯克勒庇俄斯一隻公雞。」

timeline: Mocked on stage in Aristophanes’ Clouds
阿里斯托芬在喜劇《雲》裡嘲弄他
Refuses to put an illegal motion to the vote
拒絕把違法的動議付諸表決

idea.title_en: The central idea: knowing what you do not know
idea.title_zh: 核心觀念：知道自己不知道

paras.en: Before Socrates, Greek thinkers had mostly asked what the world is made of. Socrates asked how to live, and he asked it in a new way. He assumed that anyone who is good at something can say what he is doing. A doctor can explain health; a brave man ought to be able to explain courage. When the explanation collapses under questioning, the person’s confidence has been shown to rest on nothing, and the search can start.
paras.zh: 在蘇格拉底之前，希臘思想家問的多半是世界由什麼構成。蘇格拉底問的是人該怎麼活，而且用一種新的方式問。他假定：一個人真的擅長一件事，就說得出自己在做什麼。醫生能解釋健康；勇敢的人應該能解釋勇敢。當這個解釋在追問之下垮掉，就表示這個人的自信沒有根據，而尋找可以開始了。

paras.en: Behind the method lies a bold thesis, usually called Socratic intellectualism: virtue is a kind of knowledge. If you really knew what was good for you, you would do it; so no one does wrong willingly, and all wrongdoing is a form of ignorance. That is why examining beliefs was, for him, a moral task and not an academic one.
paras.zh: 這套方法背後有一個大膽的主張，通常稱為蘇格拉底的「主知主義」：德行是一種知識。如果你真的知道什麼對自己是好的，你就會去做；所以沒有人是自願作惡的，一切過錯都是某種無知。這就是為什麼對他來說，省察信念是道德的工作，不是學院的工作。

quote.en: …the unexamined life is not worth living…
quote.note_en: Spoken after the guilty verdict, to explain why he would not accept exile on condition of silence.
quote.note_zh: 說於有罪判決之後，用來解釋他為什麼不接受「閉嘴就可以流亡」的條件。

objection.title_en: The strongest objection: weakness of will

paras.en: If virtue is knowledge, it should be impossible to know what is best and do otherwise. Yet this seems to happen every day: the smoker knows, the procrastinator knows. The Greeks called it akrasia, lack of self-mastery. Aristotle, who admired Socrates, said bluntly that the Socratic view is at odds with what we plainly observe (Nicomachean Ethics VII.2).
paras.zh: 如果德行就是知識，那麼「明知什麼最好卻不去做」應該是不可能的。可是這種事似乎天天發生：抽菸的人知道，拖延的人也知道。希臘人稱之為 akrasia，缺乏自制。亞里斯多德很敬佩蘇格拉底，卻直截了當地說，蘇格拉底的看法跟我們明明看到的事實不合（《尼各馬可倫理學》卷七第二章）。

paras.en: A Socratic can reply that the smoker does not fully know: at the moment of choice the nearer pleasure looks larger than it is, the way a nearby object looks bigger than a distant one, and what he lacks is an art of measuring (Protagoras 356c–357b). Whether that reply rescues the thesis or merely redefines “knowledge” is still disputed.
paras.zh: 蘇格拉底這一邊可以回答：抽菸的人並不是「完全知道」。在選擇的當下，近處的快樂看起來比實際大，就像近的東西看起來比遠的大；他缺的是一門「衡量的技藝」（《普羅塔哥拉篇》356c–357b）。這個回答究竟救回了原來的主張，還是只是把「知識」重新定義了一次，至今仍有爭論。

paras.en: Because Socrates wrote nothing, everything we know comes through others, and they do not agree. Aristophanes, writing while Socrates was alive, shows a ridiculous charlatan in a basket. Xenophon shows a sensible moral adviser. Plato shows a philosophical genius, and he keeps using “Socrates” as a character for decades, long after the views expressed have become Plato’s own. Scholars usually treat the early, short dialogues that end in aporia (Apology, Euthyphro, Laches) as closest to the historical man, and admit that this is a judgment and not a certainty.
paras.zh: 因為蘇格拉底什麼都沒寫，我們知道的一切都是經由別人，而這些人的說法並不一致。阿里斯托芬在蘇格拉底還活著的時候寫劇本，劇中的他是個吊在籃子裡的可笑騙子。色諾芬筆下的他，是個通情達理的道德顧問。柏拉圖筆下的他是哲學天才；而且柏拉圖把「蘇格拉底」這個角色用了幾十年，用到後來，角色口中的見解早已是柏拉圖自己的。學者通常把早期那些以困惑收場的短篇對話錄（《申辯篇》《歐緒弗洛篇》《拉凱斯篇》）視為最接近歷史上的那個人，同時也承認這是一種判斷，不是定論。

said.claim: “The only true wisdom is in knowing you know nothing.”
said.claim_zh: 「唯一真正的智慧，是知道自己一無所知。」
said.en: No ancient source has Socrates say this. It paraphrases Apology 21d and 23a–b, where he interprets the oracle to mean that human wisdom is worth little, and that the wisest person is the one who, like Socrates, recognizes this.
said.zh: 沒有任何古代文獻記載蘇格拉底說過這句話。它是《申辯篇》21d 與 23a–b 的改寫；在那裡，他把神諭解釋為：人的智慧沒什麼價值，而最有智慧的，是像蘇格拉底這樣看出這一點的人。

paras.en: The two were near contemporaries and never heard of each other. Both wrote nothing, taught by conversation, took no fee, and were remembered through dialogues composed by followers. Both held that the root of going wrong is a kind of ignorance: for Socrates, not knowing what is good; for the Buddha, avijjā, not seeing things as they are.
paras.zh: 這兩個人的年代相去不遠，彼此從未聽過對方。兩人都沒有著作，都用談話教人，都不收費，也都靠弟子編寫的對話被後人記得。兩人都認為，人走錯路的根源是某種無知：在蘇格拉底是不知道什麼是善；在佛陀是無明（avijjā），沒有如實看見事物。

paras.en: The difference shows in the remedy. For Socrates the cure is argument, and he seems to think that seeing the truth is enough to act on it. The Buddhist path adds training of attention and conduct, on the view that craving does not dissolve merely because one has reached a correct conclusion. That is, in effect, a Buddhist answer to the problem of akrasia.
paras.zh: 差別在藥方。蘇格拉底的藥是論證，而且他似乎認為，看見了真理就足以照著去做。佛教的道路多了對注意力與行為的訓練（戒與定），因為它認為，貪愛不會只因為人得出了正確的結論就消散。這其實就是佛教對「意志薄弱」問題的回答。

terms.d_en: A paid traveling teacher of rhetoric and public skill in fifth-century Greece.
terms.d_zh: 西元前五世紀希臘收費授課、教授修辭與公共事務能力的巡迴教師。

terms.d_en: His habit of professing ignorance and praising the other speaker’s expertise before testing it.
terms.d_zh: 他在檢驗對方之前，先自稱無知、稱讚對方內行的習慣。

terms.d_en: Describing teaching that draws ideas out of the learner by questions (Theaetetus 149a–151d).
terms.d_zh: 形容用提問把想法從學習者身上引出來的教法（《泰阿泰德篇》149a–151d）。

terms.d_en: Acting against one’s own better judgment.
terms.d_zh: 違背自己較好的判斷去行動。

terms.d_en: The inner sign Socrates said warned him against certain actions; it only ever said no.
terms.d_zh: 蘇格拉底說會警告他別做某些事的內在徵兆；它只會說「不」。

terms.d_en: The difficulty of recovering the historical Socrates from conflicting sources.
terms.d_zh: 從彼此衝突的史料中還原歷史上的蘇格拉底，這件事的困難。

quiz.q: How did Socrates interpret the oracle’s statement that no one was wiser than he?
options: He alone did not mistake his ignorance for knowledge.
He possessed secret knowledge from the gods.
The oracle had been bribed by Chaerephon.
Wisdom cannot be found in Athens.
Virtue is a kind of knowledge, so no one does wrong willingly.
Only intellectuals can be virtuous.
Knowledge is impossible.
Virtue cannot be defined.

quiz.q: Why is it hard to know what the historical Socrates thought?
options: He wrote nothing, and the surviving portraits disagree.
His books were burned after the trial.
Plato never mentions him.
He taught only in secret.

The other eyewitness, plainer and more practical.
